speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Could you please describe the newborn's respiratory symptoms, such as the rate, effort, and any audible sounds like grunting or wheezing?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the newborn exhibit nasal flaring, chest retractions, or grunting, and when did these signs of respiratory distress first appear? I also need to know if the baby has received surfactant therapy yet.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text:

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_X-Ray: Ground-glass appearance, air bronchograms, suggesting Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). Arterial_Blood_Gas: pH 7.30 (slightly acidic), PaCO2 50 mm Hg (elevated), PaO2 60 mm Hg (reduced), HCO3- 24 mEq/L, Base_Excess -5.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The mother had gestational diabetes. No other significant family or prenatal history. Social history: Not applicable

speaker: Patient
text: The cyanosis improves with oxygen administration. No feeding difficulties were noted prior to onset of symptoms. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The previous suggestion of a urinary tract infection is highly unlikely given the primary presentation of respiratory distress in a premature infant.
